title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a sketch of a p-adic analogue of Mumford–Tate theory in Tannakian language. It looks like a step toward Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor' problem (ICM 1970) relating p-adic Galois representations to Hodge/crystalline data. The neighbouring pages are typed text on cycle classes and purity in étale cohomology and are unrelated.

Setup:
- K is a p-adic field and π is its Galois group.
- C is a Q_p-linear rigid tensor category, 'de type fini' (tensor-generated by one object), for instance one generated by the p-adic realisations of motives.
- T_p : C → Mod_f(π, Q_p) is the étale fibre functor. Its Tannakian group is G, with α : π → G(Q_p). The image writes G(Q_ℓ), but p is meant.
- Claim: if T_p, or equivalently the functor Δ, is fully faithful, then G is the 'algebraic envelope' of α, i.e. the Zariski closure of α(π). In modern terms this is the p-adic monodromy / Mumford–Tate group.

Step 1 (Hodge–Tate side). Compose:
- T_p,
- extension of scalars to the field C = C_p (a notation clash with the category C),
- and the Hodge–Tate decomposition (Tate–Sen), landing in Mod_f(C).
The result is a bigraded fibre functor, graded by total degree (weight) and by Hodge type (p,q). By Tannakian duality this gives two commuting cocharacters i1, i2 : G_m,C → G_C. Their product i = i1·i2 is the central weight cocharacter defining the grading of C. These are the Hodge–Tate cocharacters inside the p-adic monodromy group.

Step 2 (de Rham / 'Hodge' side). There is a second bigraded 'Hodge' fibre functor T_Hdg on C, defined over K and split over some extension L. Being a fibre functor, it is given by a G_L-torsor P of isomorphisms with the étale functor: T_Hdg = P ∧^G (T_p ⊗_{Q_p} L). Its bigrading is given by cocharacters j1, j2 : G_m,L → G'_L = ad(P), the inner form of G twisted by P, with j1·j2 = i. The page ends at 'avec un isom ... T_Hdg', presumably about to compare the Hodge–Tate and Hodge data through the period torsor P.

The problem served: describing the p-adic comparison (étale ↔ Hodge/de Rham) as a torsor between two fibre functors on a motivic Tannakian category. This anticipates the period-torsor viewpoint (Fontaine, Wintenberger, Deligne).
errors: 'i(λ) = i1(λ) i2(λ) = i(λ)' is a slip; it should read i(λ) = i1(λ)·i2(λ).
The target of α should be G(Q_p), not G(Q_ℓ), since T_p is the p-adic fibre functor.

For G to be the Zariski closure of α(π), full faithfulness is not quite enough. The essential image must also be closed under subquotients in Rep(π), or one must speak of the Tannakian subcategory generated.

On the de Rham side over K one naturally has a Hodge filtration, not a grading. A bigrading (via j1, j2) exists only after splitting, so over some L. Passing from a filtration to a bigraded functor is a gap.
The letter C is used both for the tensor category and for the field C_p, which creates ambiguity.

ideas.what: The Tannakian group of the étale p-adic realisation equals the Zariski closure of the Galois image when the realisation is fully faithful.
ideas.modern_name: p-adic monodromy group / algebraic envelope of a Galois representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (l-adic algebraic envelopes, late 1960s); Saavedra Rivano (Tannakian formalism, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Tannakian formalism via Saavedra's thesis (Grothendieck's student)

ideas.what: The Hodge–Tate decomposition gives a bigraded fibre functor, hence commuting Hodge–Tate cocharacters into G_{C_p} whose product is the weight cocharacter.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Tate cocharacter inside the p-adic Mumford–Tate group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sen (1973), Serre (1979, 'Groupes algébriques associés aux modules de Hodge–Tate')

ideas.what: The de Rham/Hodge fibre functor is described as a G-torsor P twisting the étale functor, with Hodge cocharacters landing in the inner form ad(P).
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor between étale and de Rham fibre functors (p-adic comparison as a torsor)

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck sets up the 'mysterious functor' problem Tannakianly. He uses Hodge–Tate cocharacters i1, i2 in the p-adic monodromy group G_{C_p}, and Hodge cocharacters j1, j2 in the inner form ad(P) given by the étale–Hodge comparison torsor, with matching weight. This predates Sen's and Serre's work on Hodge–Tate cocharacters in Galois images and Fontaine's period-torsor formalism.
missed.quote: G_{m C} ⇉(i1,i2) G_C ... P, torseur sous G_L (T_Hdg = P ∧^G (T_p ⊗_{Q_p} L)) ... G_{m L} ⇉(j1,j2) G'_L^P = ad(P), j1(λ)j2(λ) = i(λ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence that Grothendieck framed p-adic Hodge theory as a comparison of fibre functors with cocharacter data on both sides. This is essentially the later p-adic Mumford–Tate / period-torsor picture, and it bears on the origins of the Hodge–Tate cocharacter conjectures (e.g. that the Hodge–Tate cocharacter lies in the Mumford–Tate group).

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, explicitly Tannakian formulation of p-adic Mumford–Tate groups with Hodge–Tate cocharacters and a comparison torsor whose cocharacters match in weight. The ingredients were in the air (Serre, Tate, Saavedra), and the sketch stops before any result. Still, the explicit pairing of Hodge–Tate and Hodge cocharacters across a period torsor is a notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: G(Q_ℓ) should be G(Q_p), or at least the intended meaning is the p-adic group.
'le foncteur T_p (ou, ce qui revient au même, le foncteur Δ) est pl. fidèle' — 'on' should read 'ou'.
'dans cet hom seulement)' likely reads '(dans ce cas seulement)'.
The struck/uncertain word before 'définissant la graduation de C' appears to be 'central' (the central weight homomorphism).
The page number 62 is written at the bottom left.
